AddAssets.description:
Add imported assets with the provenance their import filled in
(11.39). The only way a non-font asset enters a scene.

AddFonts.description:
Add prepared fonts and the font assets their faces need (11.13).
The only way a font enters a scene.

ApplyPreset.description: Instantiate one phase of a starter motion preset at `atFrame`.

durationMs.description:
The preset's declared `duration` parameter, in milliseconds.
Absent applies the phase at its own length.

AssetApproval.description: A named person's approval of an asset for use.

at.description:
When they approved, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp. Authoring metadata
only: nothing on the render path reads it (invariant 8).

user.description: The approving user, as the authorization layer names them (2.9).

AssetAvailability.description: Whether an asset's bytes are available where they are needed.

AssetKind.description:
The kind of thing an asset is. `Font` is here so the asset store and the
font subsystem agree on what a font asset is.

AssetLibraryItem.description:
An asset as the library knows it. Carries **both** addresses: the content
hash (immutable, addresses the store) and the project-relative path
(mutable, addresses the library). The hash is what a scene's bindings
resolve against, so re-importing over the same path — a new render of the
same logo — updates the hash but never the binding.

assetId.description: Stable scene-facing id. Survives relink; distinct from any storage id.

checksum.description: Content hash — the store address. `None` only while importing.

colorSpace.description:
The colour space an image's pixel values are in (3.17, user decision
15 Nov 2026). Set at import from the file's own tag when it has one,
otherwise by the user; never inferred (B.1). An image without one is
refused by name when drawn.

name.description: Display name, separate from the on-disk name (ADR-0002 B.3).

provenance.description:
Where the bytes came from and under what terms (11.39). Every record
carries one, and it is always written: a human-made asset may leave
every field empty, but the schema is present in every saved project.

AssetOrigin.description: Who or what produced an asset's content.

oneOf.description: A person made it, including a file a person brought into the project.

A deterministic tool derived it from other inputs: a conversion, an
export or a render.
A generative model produced it.

AssetProvenance.description: Where an asset's bytes came from and under what terms.

c2paManifest.description: An attached C2PA manifest: a project-relative path or a URI.

promptHash.description:
SHA-256 of the prompt a model was given. The prompt text is not
stored with the asset.

provider.description:
Who supplied the bytes: a font service, a stock library, a model
vendor.

sources.description:
What the asset was made or fetched from: file names, URLs, the content
hashes of input assets. Always written, so the field is visible in a
saved project even when it is empty.

BezierPath.description:
A cubic bezier path, structured like Lottie/Bodymovin's "sh" shape so it
round-trips with the web's proven vector-animation format. Segment k→k+1 is
a cubic bezier; tangents are relative to their vertex. All three arrays
must be the same length — the constraint that also makes a path animatable.

BlendMode.description:
Every blend mode the authoring vocabulary contains, supported or not.

The first ten are 1.x's `MATERIAL_BLEND_MODES`, unchanged in name and
order, because a scene authored there must mean the same thing here. 3.20
appends the rest of the Photoshop and After Effects Layer > Blending Mode
menus, so every mode a PSD, an After Effects project or a Figma file names
has exactly one variant and never a nearest neighbour. Together they are
the 27 Photoshop modes and the After Effects ones; the formulas are
EffectCraft's (`crates/color/src/blend.rs` at 9a7d3e7, MIT OR Apache-2.0),
ported with attribution in the render worker.

Two pairs share a formula and stay separate because the source menus name
them separately: `add` (After Effects) and `linear-dodge` (Photoshop's
"Linear Dodge (Add)"); `difference` and `classic-difference` differ only in
how layer opacity applies. `alpha-mask` and `inverse-alpha-mask` are After
Effects' Stencil Alpha and Silhouette Alpha under their 1.x names.

oneOf.description: After Effects Add: `b + s`, over-range kept.

The recorded live fault: 1.x's browser renderer had no `overlay`, so
it drew `screen` instead and nobody was told. It is in the vocabulary
because authors use it; it is not fixed-function, so an engine without
a shader compositing path must refuse it (invariant 18).

After Effects Stencil Alpha: the backdrop is kept where this layer is
opaque, everywhere on the stage.

After Effects Silhouette Alpha: the backdrop is cut out where this
layer is opaque, everywhere on the stage.

Photoshop and After Effects Dissolve: each pixel shows the layer or
the backdrop by a fixed per-pixel threshold against the layer's alpha.
After Effects Dancing Dissolve: Dissolve with a new pattern each frame.

After Effects Classic Color Burn: opacity fades the layer toward white
before the formula applies; negative results are kept.

After Effects Classic Color Dodge: opacity fades the layer toward
black before the formula applies.
Photoshop Linear Dodge (Add): the same formula as `add`.

After Effects Classic Difference: opacity fades the layer toward black
before the formula applies.

After Effects Stencil Luma: the backdrop is scaled by this layer's
luminance, everywhere on the stage.

After Effects Silhouette Luma: the backdrop is scaled by one minus
this layer's luminance, everywhere on the stage.
After Effects Alpha Add: source-over colour, alpha `min(sa + da, 1)`.

After Effects Luminescent Premul: source-over colour without the
layer's own alpha clipping its over-range values.

BlurDimensions.description: Which axes a blur or glow spreads along.

useLegacy.description:
After Effects' legacy linear formula, which clips; otherwise tone
curves that keep black and white fixed.

ColorValue.description:
An authored paint: nothing, a colour, or a gradient.

`None` is a value, not an absence — "the author turned the fill off" and
"the author has not set a fill" are different states, and collapsing them
is how a transparent object becomes a black one on the other renderer.
Ported from 1.x `ColorValue`, with every colour now tagged.

angle.description: Degrees, clockwise from the positive X axis.

ContentHash.description: Content address of asset bytes: SHA-256, lowercase hex.

ControlField.description: One named property an operator is allowed to fill on a template.

ControlFieldKind.description: The kind of value an operator may enter for a declared field.

ControlValue.description: A typed value supplied to a declared control field.

CreateShape.description:
Create a shape from a bezier path (3.13). The path's own coordinates
place it; its fill is grey and its stroke off until `setPaint` and
`setStroke` say otherwise.

compoundPaths.description:
Additional subpaths, drawn with the primary path as one
compound shape under its fill rule; absent or empty is one path.

CubicBezier.description:
Cubic-bezier control points for a custom outgoing easing.

`x1` and `x2` stay in 0–1 because they are time controls; y may overshoot
provided the resulting segment stays within the property's range (opacity
0–1, width/height non-negative). Other properties permit overshoot.
The points are stored with the
key, not solved from neighbouring keys at display time, so a saved scene
means the same curve when it is reopened.

CurvePoint.description: A control point of a tone curve, both coordinates 0–1.

Curves.description:
Curves: each channel is a monotone cubic through its points (at least
two), extended linearly beyond the end points. Colour channels go through
the RGB curve first, then their own.

EditProperty.description: A property value edit; with `autoKey` it also upserts a key at `frame`.

EditorModule.description:
The Editor module a gesture came from (11.37). Undo scoped to a module
reverses only batches tagged with it; an untagged batch belongs to
`Scene`. The surface that issues a gesture names its own module, because
guessing it from edit kinds would misfile a gesture that touches several.

EffectInstance.description: One entry in an object's effect stack.

effectId.description:
Stable within the object: keyframe channels address the effect by it,
so reordering the stack keeps every channel valid.

enabled.description: A disabled effect is skipped entirely. Keyframable with hold keys.

EffectPoint.description: A point in the layer's own pixels.

EmbeddingPolicy.description:
Whether a font's bytes may travel inside a `.gpxpkg` — the licensing
decision made per font (docs/p2-licensing-positions.md §5).

oneOf.description: Bytes may be packaged (licence permits redistribution: OFL, Apache…).
Package carries the reference; the render node resolves and caches.
Workstation-only; bytes never leave the operator's machine.

Exposure.description: Exposure, in linear light whatever the working space.

Fill.description: Paints the layer's pixels with a colour, keeping their coverage.

opacity.description: 0–1: how much of the colour replaces the layer's own.

FontDefinition.description:
A family as the scene knows it: its faces, fallbacks and licensing
posture. Embedded verbatim in the scene document, so a package is
self-describing.

license.description:
The declared licence. A `Package` font without one is a preflight
refusal (p2-licensing-positions §5: unstated licence ⇒ restricted).

FontFaceDefinition.description: One face of a family: weight/style/stretch with a source.

FontFormat.description:
Font container formats the pipeline accepts. WOFF/WOFF2 are delivery
wrappers; the shaper sees the same tables either way.

FontLoadStatus.description:
Load state of a font or face. `Missing` at preflight is a refusal
(`Refusal::FontMissing`), never a fallback to a system font.

oneOf.description: Linked source declared but not yet resolved; cannot preflight.

FontSource.description:
Where a face's bytes come from.

`rename_all_fields` (not `rename_all`) because the variant *fields* are
what hit the wire: `rename_all` alone would leave `asset_id` snake_case
while every other contract is camelCase.

oneOf.description: Packaged asset bytes, content-addressed.

originalUrl.description: Original public URL when this face was resolved and cached from CSS.

stylesheetUrl.description: Stylesheet that declared this cached face.

oneOf.description: A CSS stylesheet declaring `@font-face` rules (Google Fonts class).
An Adobe Fonts project. Reference-only by licence; never packaged.
A direct HTTPS font file URL.

GradientCoordinateMode.description:
Whether a gradient's coordinates are the object's or the scene's. An
object-space gradient follows its object; a scene-space one stays put
while the object moves through it.

GradientSpread.description: What a gradient does outside its 0–1 span. CSS's own names.

Invert.description: Invert: `1 - v` on the chosen channels, blended back toward the original.

blendWithOriginal.description: 0–1: how much of the original comes back; 0 is a full inversion.

Levels.description:
Levels: the RGB controls map every colour channel, then each channel's
own; the alpha controls map coverage where the layer drew.

clipToOutputBlack.description: Clip values below input black / above input white.

LicenseClass.description:
The terms an asset may be used under, as a class a show profile can test
(13.8) rather than free licence text.

oneOf.description: Made by or for the production, which holds the rights.
Third-party, licensed for commercial broadcast.

An open licence that permits commercial use: OFL, CC0, CC BY,
Apache-2.0, MIT.
GPL-class: obligations attach when it is redistributed.
Licensed for non-commercial use only, such as CC BY-NC.
Licensed for editorial or news use only.
Limited by territory, term or medium.

Mask.description: One layer mask (3.19): a closed path in the object's own coordinates.

expansion.description:
Grows (positive) or shrinks (negative) the mask outward from its
path, in pixels.

feather.description:
Softens the edge: a Gaussian blur of the mask's coverage, in pixels
(the blur's standard deviation is half of it).

MaskMode.description: How a mask combines with the masks above it (3.19), After Effects' modes.

oneOf.description: Ignored: the mask is kept but shapes nothing.
Union with the masks above.
Removes its area from the masks above.
Keeps only where it overlaps the masks above.
Keeps where exactly one of it and the masks above covers.

ObjectField.description:
A typed inspector field/value pair. The adjacent tag makes an invalid field
and value combination unrepresentable on the command wire.

oneOf.description:
The object's box (`ObjectBase.width`, `height`): a rect and an image
fill it, an ellipse is inscribed in it, paragraph text wraps inside it.
Finite and not negative, as the engine draws it.
Draw order within a layer (`ObjectBase.z_index`).

PaintSlot.description: Which of an object's two paints `SetPaint` sets.

PhaseKind.description:
The operator phases a scene timeline can name.

These are exactly `crate::mcp::MOTION_PHASES`, and a test below pins them
against it: a phase added to one and not the other fails the gate rather
than producing a scene the agent surface cannot describe.

oneOf.description: Build on. Triggered by Take.
Idle loop after `in` completes. Interruptible at any frame.
Build off. Triggered by Out.
A staged build, triggered by Continue. A timeline may carry several.
How a bound value changes on air without a full re-take.

Posterize.description: Posterize: each colour channel snaps to `level` evenly spaced values.

ProvenanceTool.description: The tool, or for model origin the model, that made or imported the bytes.

RationalRate.description:
A frame rate as an exact rational. Never a float (invariant 12).

29.97 is 30000/1001 and cannot be represented in binary floating point.
Accumulating a rounded rate across an 8-hour soak drifts the clock, so this
type deliberately offers no `f64` constructor.

RelinkAsset.description: Point a library asset at new bytes, keeping its id and bindings.

RelinkMaterial.description: Repoint every use of one material to another.

RemoveFont.description:
Remove one font nothing names, with the font assets no other font
uses. The only way a font leaves a scene.

ReplaceControl.description: Replace the declared control with the same `fieldId`.

ReplaceFont.description:
Replace a font's faces and files under the same id (11.13): what
names the font keeps naming it, and its display name, fallbacks
and enabled state are kept.

Revision.description:
Publish revision. Exact-match only: a take against a stale revision is
refused, never coerced (invariant 17).

Rgba.description:
A colour, with the space it was authored in.

Components are 0–1 floats rather than 8-bit bytes because the working
space is linear and 8 bits of linear has visible banding in the shadows.

SceneEasing.description:
The easing between two keys. Closed and finite: the curve an author chooses
must be one every evaluator knows by name, because a substituted curve is a
visual change no one named (invariant 18).

SceneEdit.description:
One change to one scene document. Only carried inside
`EditorCommand::EditScene` and only applied through [`apply_edits`].

SceneKeyframe.description: One key on one numeric property channel.

bezier.description: Custom bezier control points, present exactly when easing is custom.

easing.description: Outgoing easing toward the next key.

frame.description: Absolute frame at the scene canvas rate.

value.description: The property's value at that frame, in the property's own units.

SceneTarget.description:
The document an edit batch applies to: an open session, or a scene in the
project store (read, edited and written back in one command).

SessionKey.description:
Identity of one open editor session. A `u32`, so TS receives `number`
rather than `bigint` (memory rule 22). Keys are monotonic from 1.

SetAnchor.description:
Set the pivot every listed object rotates and scales about; left
out is the object's origin. Refuses a non-finite point by name.

SetAssetColorSpace.description:
Tag the colour space an image asset's pixel values are in (3.17):
what an untagged image needs before it can be drawn.

SetBinding.description: Bind `property` to a data path, or unbind it when `path` is absent.

SetBlendMode.description:
Set the layer blend mode of every listed object (3.20); left out
is `normal`. A kind that draws nothing itself (a group, a layer, a
marker, a camera, a light) refuses `objectFieldNotApplicable`.

SetCanvas.description:
Change the canvas: its rational frame rate and/or its size (11.43).
Frames are canonical (invariant 12): a rate change keeps every key
frame number and the duration in frames, so the graphic plays the
same frames at the new rate; only its wall-clock length changes.

SetClipChild.description:
Name a group's clip child, or clear it by leaving `clipChildId` out
(3.19). The clip child must be one of the group's own children and
draw pixels (`clipGroupInvalid`).

SetEffects.description:
Replace one object's ordered effect stack (3.22); empty clears it.
Each effect is checked as the validator checks it (`effectInvalid`).

SetGroupChildren.description:
Replace a group's ordered children (3.19). A child another group
already claims, a missing child and a cycle refuse
`sceneHierarchyInvalid`; a group is the only kind with children here.

SetObjectField.description: One inspector field over every listed object.

SetObjectMasks.description:
Replace one object's mask list; an empty list clears it (3.19).
Each mask refuses by name (`maskInvalid`, with its index) when the
engine cannot draw it as authored.

SetPaint.description:
Set one paint of every listed object to a colour or gradient, or
clear it by leaving `paint` out (3.17). A shape's fill or stroke
switch follows the paint.

SetSceneId.description: Change the id of a scene that is not bound to a stored origin.

SetShapePath.description:
Replace a shape's geometry: its path and every additional subpath
(a compound path); an empty list leaves one path. `fill_rule`, when
given, decides where overlapping subpaths fill (even-odd cuts a
hole); left out keeps the shape's rule.

SetStroke.description:
Set the stroke width and style of every listed object (3.17). A
style left out is the default: miter joins, butt caps, solid.

SetTrackMatte.description:
Set one object's track matte by its source's id, or clear it by
leaving `trackMatte` out (3.19). Refuses by name
(`trackMatteInvalid`) what cannot be drawn as authored.

SetTrim.description:
Set one shape's trim window (3.13): start and end in percent of the
path, offset in percent of a turn. A value left out is its default
(0, 100, 0); all three replace what the shape had.

SourceColorSpace.description:
What a colour or a texture was authored in. There is no `Unknown`: an
untagged source is a defect the importer must refuse, not a value a
renderer may guess at (B.1, "never infer").

oneOf.description:
IEC 61966-2-1. What a hex literal, a PNG without an ICC profile and
most authoring tools mean.
Already linear — no decode on the way in.
ITU-R BT.709 with its own transfer curve. Broadcast source material.

StrokeCap.description: How a stroke ends an open path and each dash. SVG's and CSS's names.

StrokeJoin.description: How a stroke joins its segments. The names are SVG's and CSS's.

StrokeStyle.description:
A stroke's joins, caps and dash pattern (3.17). Lengths are in the
object's own units, like `strokeWidth`.

dash.description: Alternating dash and gap lengths; empty is a solid line.

dashOffset.description: How far into the dash pattern the stroke starts.

miterLimit.description: A miter join longer than this many stroke widths becomes a bevel.

StyleColor.description:
A text-style colour, either literal or resolved from the active project
design system when the style is applied.

StyleNumber.description:
A numeric text-style value, either literal or resolved from the active
project design system when the style is applied.

TextCase.description:
Case applied when the text is drawn, not when it is typed: the authored
characters stay as they are, so a data binding can replace the text and
the case still applies, and switching it off returns the author's own
capitalisation.

TextStyle.description:
A named, reusable subset of a text object's appearance.

Optional entries are deliberately absent rather than defaults: applying a
style must not overwrite a property its author did not declare.

Threshold.description: Threshold: pixels at or above `level` luminance become white, the rest black.

TimelinePhase.description: One named span of the scene timeline.

endFrame.description: One past the last frame. See the module note on why this is exclusive.

name.description:
Distinguishes several `continue` phases from each other. Absent means
the kind names it uniquely, which is true of every kind but `continue`.

startFrame.description: First frame of the phase, inclusive.

Tint.description: Maps luminance to a colour ramp between two colours.

TokenRef.description:
A token reference in a preset: `{duration.base}`, `{easing.brand-in}`.

A preset that hardcodes a value instead of referencing a token is a bug for
the same reason a component hardcoding a hex colour is (G.6.1). Kept as a
string with a checked shape rather than a free string, so a malformed
reference is caught at parse, not at render.

TrackMatte.description: A layer's track matte (3.19): its source by explicit id, and the mode.

TrackMatteMode.description:
What a track matte takes from its source (3.19), After Effects' modes.
Luma is the Rec.709 weighting of the source's premultiplied working-space
colour, so a transparent source counts as black; values clamp to 0..1.

oneOf.description: The layer shows where the source is opaque.
The layer shows where the source is transparent.
The layer shows where the source is bright.
The layer shows where the source is dark.

UpdateFont.description:
Change a font's display name, fallbacks or enabled state (11.13).
Switching off a font something names is refused, as removing it is.

UpdateKeyframe.description: Replace a key that already exists at `keyframe.frame`.

Vibrance.description:
Vibrance: saturation weighted `(1 - s) * min(s, 0.5)`: a grey and a fully
saturated colour are left alone, and a half-saturated one gains most.

description:
Apply an ordered, atomic edit batch to one document. One batch is
one undo entry, tagged with the module that issued it.

Against a stored scene the batch is a compare-and-swap (8.12):
`if_revision` is the revision the caller read, the write lands only
if that is still the stored scene's revision, and the outcome
carries the new one. The MCP surface requires it for a stored
target; a session target has no stored revision and must not name
one.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. A fresh string per logical write. Repeating the call with the same key and the same arguments returns the first answer without writing again, so a retry after a timeout cannot duplicate. The same key with other arguments refuses idempotencyKeyReused.
